instruction: Choose a suitable finite-element simulation tool available in the current Windows fused environment. The task must be completed through an interactive graphical workflow. Use the selected finite-element simulation tool to perform a modal analysis of a cantilever beam (Variant B). Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a 14 mm x 8 mm rectangle in the Y-Z plane and extrude along the global X-axis to a length of 360 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3, and density = 7.95e-9 tonne/mm^3. Create a Solid Homogeneous section using Steel and assign it to the entire beam. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the beam. Analysis Step: Create a Linear Perturbation Frequency step named Step-Modal-B. Request 5 eigenvalues. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply an Encastre boundary condition to the fixed end face at X = 0. Discretization: Mesh the beam with a global seed size of 10 mm. Assign the element type appropriate three-dimensional solid element formulation and generate the mesh. Job Execution: Create a job named Job-Modal-B, submit it for analysis, and wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and native solver result artifact on the Desktop.
